key_insight: Organic semiconductor performance is strongly shaped by weak intermolecular forces and interface-driven supramolecular ordering, so controlling assembly can tune electronic behavior.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and engineering interfaces offers a practical route to improve organic photovoltaic and other organic electronic device performance beyond what molecular structure alone predicts.
method: Review of recent studies on supramolecular assembly at organic-semiconductor interfaces
Focus on how interface symmetry breaking influences molecular orientation and electronic properties
Survey of computer simulations used to model assembly and orientational anisotropy
evidence_signal: The abstract summarizes a literature review rather than reporting new experimental datasets, and it highlights consistent advances and open challenges across transistors, LEDs, and photovoltaics.
watch_item: Device behavior is still hard to predict from chemical structure alone because disorder and weak non-covalent interactions can dominate interface outcomes.
paper_title: The interplay of interfaces, supramolecular assembly, and electronics in organic semiconductors
